📚 Today you learned

Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) & Net New ARR

ARR annualizes a subscription business's recurring revenue run-rate, stripping out one-time deals so you can see the real base. It's why CrowdStrike ripped +20.5% today (movers section above): ARR hit $5.84B (+25% YoY), but the number that actually moved the stock was net new ARR — $332.8M added this quarter, itself accelerating versus the prior quarter. That's the growth-of-growth signal SaaS investors price off, more than the headline EPS beat. It touches your GOOG position indirectly — Google Cloud and Workspace both run on subscription/consumption revenue, and the market increasingly values that segment on an ARR-style multiple rather than blended company P/E. When you see ARR in a report, ask two things: is it growing, and is net-new ARR accelerating or decelerating quarter over quarter — the second one is the real tell.

Also today: land-and-expand — the SaaS growth motion of landing a small initial contract then expanding seat count/usage over time; it's what makes net-new ARR compound faster than new-logo count alone.
